facts.text: Only two major-college teams of the 1940s allowed 350 points: New Mexico State (1948: 391 allowed, 3-7); BYU (1949: 372 allowed, 0-11).
The only major-college team of the 1940s to allow 20 or fewer points all season (8+ games): Randolph Field, 1944 — 19 allowed in 12 games.
The only major-college team of the 1940s to score 20 or fewer points all season (7+ games): San Francisco, 1943 — 13 points in 8 games, 1-7.
The only major-college team of the 1940s to lose 11 games: BYU, 1949 — 0-11.
Army had 3 perfect seasons in the 1940s, more than any other program. (1944, 1945, 1949)
Most 300-point seasons in the 1940s: Georgia, 5 (1941, 1942, 1945, 1946, 1948).
Most 8-win seasons in the 1940s: Notre Dame, 7.
Most 8-loss seasons in the 1940s: Kansas State, 5 (1942, 1946, 1947, 1948, 1949).
8 major-college teams scored 380 points in the 1940s (10 seasons). The most extreme: Second Air Force, 1944 — 513 points, 10-4-1.
8 major-college teams outscore opponents by 300 in the 1940s (9 seasons). The most extreme: Randolph Field, 1944 — 508-19.
Most points by a team in a season in the 1940s: Second Air Force, 1944 — 513 (10-4-1).
Fewest points allowed in a season (8+ games) in the 1940s: Randolph Field, 1944 — 19.
Most losses in a season in the 1940s: BYU, 1949 — 0-11.
Worst scoring margin in a season in the 1940s: Columbia, 1943 — outscored 313-33.
Biggest scoring margin in a season in the 1940s: Randolph Field, 1944 — 508-19.
Most wins in a season in the 1940s: Randolph Field, 1944 — 12-0.
16 major-college teams went unbeaten and untied (8+ games) in the 1940s (22 seasons). The most extreme: Randolph Field, 1944 — 12-0, 508-19 on the season.
21 major-college teams won 10 games in the 1940s (25 seasons). The most extreme: Randolph Field, 1944 — 12-0.
9 major-college teams lost every game (7+ games) in the 1940s (10 seasons). The most extreme: BYU, 1949 — 0-11, outscored 372-105.
10 major-college teams went unbeaten but not untied (6+ games) in the 1940s (13 seasons). The most extreme: Mississippi State, 1940 — 10-0-1.
9 major-college teams tied 3 games in the 1940s. The most extreme: Auburn, 1949 — 2-4-3.

shortNote: Player statistics in the college record begin in 1956; every line here is from team seasons, the only complete record for these years. Nothing was padded.
method: College football: each line is one Stathead (Sports Reference college football) Season Finder query over the decade, run in a signed-in subscriber session; result rows and stable ids are stored as provenance. Counts cover the database's major-college (today's FBS) programs, the scope of Sports Reference's college records.

Player statistics begin in 1956; decades before that are built from team seasons (record, points for and against), which run back to 1869. The 2026 season is in progress and excluded. Defensive stats such as sacks and tackles appear only in recent decades, and rules on them return nothing earlier.
